title: SPVR: syntax-to-prompt vulnerability repair based on large language models

key_numbers.metric: Pass@3 repairs (ChatGPT-4, with vs without SPVR)
Ablation Pass@3 (ChatGPT-3.5-turbo, with vs without MET info)

structure_gain: Removing MET-derived (AST-diff) syntax info dropped pass@3 from 138/547 to 55/547 on ChatGPT-3.5-turbo, same model/samples/metric (Table 10, Sec 5.4) -- roughly 151% relative gain from the structured syntax cues.
stop_detail: Generated patches are constrained by matching the parsed output against the identified MET subtree during regeneration (Section 3.4) -- a syntactic well-formedness filter, not semantic or formal verification.

title: Code Vulnerability Repair with Large Language Model using Context-Aware Prompt Tuning
structure_gain: Repair success rises from 15% (no context) to 63% (full context-aware prompt combining CWE knowledge + structured code-context cues), a >4x improvement, same LLM (Copilot) throughout (Table I).
stop_detail: Grounding is purely prompt-based: CWE description plus four structured code-context cues (buffer identification, bound selection, range precision, suitable placement) are progressively appended in a 'waterfall' staged prompt (Sections III-IV); no AST/CFG extraction performed.

title: Benchmarking LLMs and LLM-based Agents in Practical Vulnerability Detection for Code Repositories

key_numbers.metric: pAcc improvement of ReAct over Plain LLM

structure_gain: ReAct agent (interprocedural tool-use context via get_callers/get_callees/get_definition) raises pairwise accuracy from ~1-17.6% (Plain LLM) up to 19.13% (ReAct+CoT), but plain LLM retains higher raw F1 (65.96 vs 57-58), so the gain is metric-dependent (results table).
stop_detail: ReAct agent grounds interprocedural reasoning via three callable tools built from CFlow-derived call graphs and CTags-extracted function bodies (get_callers, get_callees, get_definition), adaptively pulling context in a thought-action-observation loop (ReAct methodology section).

title: Minimizing False Positives in Static Bug Detection via LLM-Enhanced Path Feasibility Analysis

key_numbers.value: FPR_P 0.98-1.0 per bug type (NPD 0.98, BOF 1.0, UAF 1.0); the 72-96% range describes FPR_R, a different metric

structure_gain: vs LLM4SA baseline (broad context, no localized constraint analysis), same GPT-4o-mini/dataset/temperature=0: NPD FPR_R 0.51 -> 0.72 (+41.2% relative, Table 1); vs LLMDFA (exhaustive path traversal): NPD FPR_R 0.35 -> 0.72 (+105.7%).
stop_detail: The reasoning/solving loop halts when Z3 returns UNSAT or after a max of 5 context-retrieval iterations / 3 solver-error-fix rounds (Sections 3.2.2, 3.3) -- solver-grounded termination, not mere LLM self-report.

title: VULSOLVER: Vulnerability Detection via LLM-Driven Constraint Solving
structure_gain: vs CWE-DF (LLM-only baseline, no constraint-solving structure): 48-52% accuracy vs VULSOLVER's 96.64-98.41% (Table IV) -- but this is confounded with a different LLM-prompting architecture, not representation alone.
stop_detail: Verification is a final logical check of the derived sink parameter state S_n against Trigger Constraints (Phi_tg) once the last subtask's state is obtained (Sections III-C3, II-D2) -- self-contained symbolic evaluation, no external SMT solver.

title: LLM-Driven Adaptive Source-Sink Identification and False Positive Mitigation for Static Analysis
structure_gain: Neuro-symbolic loop (LLM source/sink inference + taint-path/CFG constraint validation) improves F1 to 79.6 vs 77.8 (IRIS) and 66.4 (static-only), cutting FPR to 17.5% vs 38.7% static-only (Table 1); no isolated raw-text-vs-structured ablation is reported.
stop_detail: LLM classifies candidate functions as source/sink/neutral from code snippets plus retrieved API docs, commit history, and comments; a separate constraint-validation stage checks static features (path length, sanitizer presence, control-flow feasibility) and a trained classifier filters spurious alerts, explicitly 'to avoid overreliance on LLMs' (neuro-symbolic architecture section).

title: An Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Approaches for Code Vulnerability Detection: RAG, SFT, and Dual-Agent Systems
structure_gain: RAG (retrieved MITRE CWE-database context) reaches 0.85 F1 vs the un-augmented base LLaMA-3.2-3B baseline's 0.67 F1 (+0.18); however RAG, SFT, and Dual-Agent each add a different, confounded mechanism atop the same base model rather than a pure representation-only swap
stop_detail: RAG grounds responses in the MITRE CWE database via top-20-chunk retrieval + re-ranking (§III-C); the Dual-Agent's second agent audits the first agent's reasoning for logical inconsistencies and unsupported assumptions (§III-E)

title: VulnAgent-R2: Evidence-Calibrated Multi-Agent Auditing for Repository-Level Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.metric: F1 ablation on PrimeVul, full vs. w/o graph optimizer

structure_gain: Full VulnAgent-R2 (bounded graph-context optimizer) vs. w/o graph optimizer, same base LLM (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B), on PrimeVul: F1 0.385 vs. 0.337 (Table 10); w/o CER 0.359, w/o Sceptic 0.352, w/o VPS 0.346 -- each context/verification component contributes measurably.
stop_detail: Grounded via a Joern-style code property graph (AST+CFG+DFG+CALL edges) traversed under a token-budgeted, greedy utility-maximizing selection (Eq. 6) that pulls in callers, callees, data-flow neighbors, tests, configs, and historical patches; claims are further calibrated via counterfactual evidence reweighting and executable verification harnesses (graph triage / CER / VPS sections).

title: QASecClaw: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach for False Positive Reduction in Static Application Security Testing

key_numbers.metric: false positives, QASecClaw vs. standalone Semgrep

key_numbers.value: 87.1% vs standalone Semgrep 90.0% (-2.9pp; the paper's '3.2%' is the relative reduction)

stop_detail: The SAST Filter Agent builds a per-finding prompt containing the CWE category, file location, and the complete relevant source-file text (batched 15 files at a time), queries Qwen 3.5 Plus, and parses a structured JSON true/false-positive verdict (Methodology section).

title: RAVEN: Agentic RAG for Automated Vulnerability Repair

key_numbers.metric: out-of-distribution repair success rate (Vul4J, 23 unseen CWEs)

structure_gain: No ablation isolates the retrieval/Curator-Agent context contribution; authors report only end-to-end repair success rate vs. other repair tools (Table III: RAVEN 7/9 correct vs. fewer for SAN2PATCH/PatchAgent on unseen C vulnerabilities), so no representation-only delta is available.
stop_detail: A Curator Agent iteratively calls repository-exploration tools (read_bundle, search_repo, find_symbol, read_file) to gather cross-file caller/callee and dependency information, combined with a multi-faceted BM25 retriever (keyword, code-snippet, and Joern-CPG based) whose top patch is chosen by a Selector Agent and injected into the Patch Generator's prompt (Algorithm 1 / Curator Agent section).

title: AgenticRepair: Multi-Faceted Program Context Engineering for Agentic Vulnerability Repair

key_numbers.value: 75.0% on 200-CVE strict subset; abstract reports 73% overall, outperforming strongest baseline by 29pp
w/o code-structure -1.5pp, w/o execution context -0.5pp, w/o commit-history -2.0pp (75.0% -> 73.0-74.5%)

structure_gain: Removing any single context facet (code-structure/data-flow, runtime-execution, or commit-history) costs only 0.5-2pp success rate (75.0%->73.0-74.5%) on the same model (GPT-5.2) and multi-agent scaffold, showing the three facets are complementary rather than individually dominant; collapsing to a single-agent scaffold costs 44.5pp
stop_detail: Repair subagent's synthesis-verification loop stops when the AddressSanitizer/sanitizer reproduction harness reports no violation, or after a 75-step budget is exhausted (synthesis-verification loop description)
